explain.say: On a stone in a churchyard, a sword, and the words: rightwise king born of all England. A boy pulls it out. That boy is Arthur. Sir Thomas Malory, a knight writing in prison, finished this great English prose book around 1470. The timeline shows the story from rise to fall.

explain.say: Look at the third event. Arthur marries Guinevere, and the Round Table becomes a fellowship of the best knights in the world. Malory gathered French romances into English prose and made one long story. What makes a fellowship like this so fragile?

explain.say: Here are the people inside the story. Arthur's queen is loved by his best knight, Lancelot. Mordred is Arthur's son by his half-sister. And when Lancelot kills Gawain's brothers by accident, a feud begins. Which link on the board will break the table?

Look at events five and six. The Grail quest takes the best knights away; Galahad succeeds and many die. Then Agravaine and Mordred trap Lancelot with the queen, and civil war follows. Did love or loyalty destroy Camelot?

explain.say: At Camlann, Arthur and Mordred strike each other down. Bedivere throws Excalibur back into the lake, and Arthur is carried away to Avalon. Look at the real timeline too: Caxton printed it in 1485. Wonderful work. Challenge: decide who is most to blame, and argue it.

faq.a: Probably Sir Thomas Malory of Newbold Revel in Warwickshire, a knight imprisoned several times for violent crimes and politics. He finished the book in prison around 1470.

faq.q: Why does the Round Table fall?
faq.a: Divided loyalties: the Grail quest kills many knights, Lancelot and Guinevere are exposed, Lancelot kills Gawain's brothers in a rescue, and Mordred seizes the throne while Arthur is at war.
asks: What causes the fall of Camelot?

faq.a: Arthur's son by his half-sister Morgause. He helps expose Lancelot and Guinevere, takes the throne while Arthur is away, and he and Arthur kill each other at Camlann.

faq.q: What is the Holy Grail quest in Malory?
faq.a: A spiritual quest for the cup of the Last Supper. Most knights fail; Galahad, the purest, achieves it with Percival and Bors, but the quest scatters the fellowship.
A manuscript of Malory's work discovered at Winchester College in 1934. It is earlier than Caxton's printed edition and shows how Caxton edited the text.

facts: William Caxton printed Le Morte d'Arthur in 1485.
The Winchester Manuscript of Malory was discovered in 1934.
Malory says he finished the work in the ninth year of Edward IV's reign, 1469 to 1470.
